name: Vitex negundo (five-leaved chaste tree)
short: Rats: Vitex negundo leaf extract lowered paracetamol blood levels. Low back pain: one 30-day trial randomising 72 adults to a blend of it with ginger or placebo reported no significant adverse events.
text: Few human safety data were found. In a 30-day randomised, placebo-controlled trial in which 72 adults aged 18 to 60 with low back pain were randomised 1:1 to a blend of Vitex negundo leaves and ginger rhizome taken by mouth or to placebo, the blend was assessed for safety by adverse-event reporting, and no significant adverse event was reported; the result cannot be attributed to Vitex negundo alone. The remaining evidence is from animal studies. In rats given Vitex negundo leaf extract by mouth daily for six days, paracetamol given on days 3 and 6 reached significantly lower blood levels, with a greater fall at higher extract doses, and the extent of its absorption and its relative bioavailability were significantly reduced; this is the only interaction named in the cited sources and has not been tested in people in these sources. In mice, a butanol extract of Vitex negundo showed no signs of nerve impairment or acute behavioural toxicity, with a median lethal dose above 5000 mg/kg. Applied to the skin of rats for 90 days, Vitex negundo essential oil caused no behavioural, blood, organ or tissue changes.
